description: We're high school students from Poland. One of us found asteroids with NASA, one represented Poland at NASA Space Camp, one launches his own rockets, and the rest of us want to build space companies. We made the app we wish we'd had when we were kids.
summary:
SPHERExium is a web app that lets anyone, from a child to a grandparent, in engaging way discover moving objects in real NASA SPHEREx data. SPHEREx scans the whole sky in 102 infrared bands and new data arrives constantly, which is far more than a few scientists can inspect. We open that data to everyone.

Users start with a short tutorial: three frames of the same patch of sky taken on different days. Most dots stay still, but one moves. Finding it is citizen science in under a minute. Users can then choose their own field of view, add or subtract images taken at different times to reveal motion, explore the infrared bands, overlay Gaia and WISE catalogues to check whether an object is already known, and read metadata such as contamination flags. Every view has its own URL with coordinates, so it can be shared or embedded. The app is built to update with the latest SPHEREx releases. Finally, users can create a postcard with their favourite galaxy or a newly discovered object.

SPHERExium removes the barrier to entering the space sector and citizen science: no degree, no telescope, no experience needed. It inspires young people early, helps teachers bring real NASA data into class, and adds thousands of extra eyes to the search for moving objects such as Planet X candidates.
details:
HOW IT WORKS

The frontend is built in React with TypeScript (TSX). The backend is Python with FastAPI, which fetches SPHEREx sky frames for the chosen coordinates and time range and serves them to the app. Users scrub through frames on a timeline, and a moving object reveals itself against the fixed stars. Each view is stored in a URL, so any patch of sky can be shared or embedded.

USER EXPERIENCE

A three-step tutorial teaches motion detection by doing. Next, users explore real data, name their find and generate a postcard of a favourite galaxy or new object.

BENEFITS

Zero entry barrier: no degree, no telescope, no experience. Teachers get a ready classroom activity on real NASA data.

INTENDED IMPACT

Early inspiration, more people in citizen science, and a more diverse path into the space sector.

CREATIVITY

We replaced dense scientific interfaces with a guided, game-like journey, and turned a discovery into a personal postcard.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Simplicity for every age and device - Fast loading: small fields of view for quick transfer - Scientific honesty: findings are labelled as candidates, not confirmed discoveries - Easy updates as new SPHEREx data is released

Hardware: laptops and phones. Design: Canva.
